{{Short description|American physicist (1937–2025)}}
'''Allen Marshall Goldman''' (October 18, 1937 – May 16, 2025) was an American experimental [[condensed matter physicist]], known for his research on electronic transport properties of [[superconductor]]s<ref name=BuckleyPrize>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Goldman&first_nm=Allen&year=2015|title=2015 Oliver E. Buckley Prize Recipient, Allen Goldman|website=American Physical Society}}</ref> and for the eponymous Carlson-Goldman mode involving collective oscillations in superconductors.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Artemenko, S. N.|author2=Volkov, A. F.|year=1997|title=Collective oscillations in superconductors revisited|eprint=cond-mat/9712086 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Carlson, R. V.|author2=Goldman, A. M.|title=Propagating order-parameter collective modes in superconducting films|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=34|issue=1|year=1975|pages=11–15|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.11|bibcode=1975PhRvL..34...11C }}</ref>

==Life and career==
Goldman was born on October 18, 1937.<ref>biographical information from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> He graduated in 1954 from the [[Bronx High School of Science]] and received in 1958 his bachelor's degree in physics and chemistry from [[Harvard University]]. In 1965, he graduated from [[Stanford University]] with a Ph.D. in physics.<ref name=nas>{{cite web|title=Allen M. Goldman|website=National Academy of Sciences|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/allen-m-goldman-t2omq9/}}</ref> His Ph.D. thesis ''Properties of superconductors and selected magnetic materials in the configuration of thin films'' was supervised by [[William M. Fairbank]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Allen M. Goldman|website=Physics Tree|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=285455}}</ref>

Goldman became in 1965 an assistant professor in the physics department of the [[University of Minnesota]]. From 1966 to 1970, he was a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]]. In the 1970s, he discovered, with his doctoral student Richard V. Carlson,<ref>{{cite book |author=Carlson, Richard Vernal |url=https://www.osti.gov/biblio/4187343 |title=Order parameter fluctuations and collective modes in superconductors, ''No. COO-1569-128'' |publisher=University of Minnesota |year=1975 |location=Minneapolis |doi=10.2172/4187343 |osti=4187343}}</ref> collective oscillations (Carlson-Goldman modes) in thin superconducting films. Such modes are coupled collective oscillations of a thin superconducting film's superconducting part (''i.e.'' Cooper pairs) and the film's quasiparticles. Goldman was one of the pioneers in the study of [[phase transition]]s in two-dimensional systems, including the [[Kosterlitz-Thouless transition]] in thin superconducting films and networks of [[Josephson effect|Josephson transitions]]. There he was a full professor from 1975 to 1992 and an Institute of Technology Distinguished Professor from 1992 to 2008 with appointment to regent's professor in 2008. Goldman was elected in 1982 a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Historic Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic |website=American Association for the Advancement of Science}} (search on last name "Goldman")</ref> in 1984 a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1984&unit_id=&institution=University+of+Minnesota,+Minneapolis |website=American Physical Society}} (search on year=1984 and institution=university of Minnesota, Minneapolis)</ref> and in 2007 a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]. He was also the head of the University of Minnesota's school of physics and astronomy from 1996 to 2009.<ref name=AIP>{{cite web|title=Allen M. Goldman|website=American Institute of Physics|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11511023.html}}</ref> He became regents professor emeritus.<ref name="Allen Goldman">{{cite web|title=Allen Goldman|website=School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Minnesota|url=https://cse.umn.edu/physics/allen-goldman}}</ref>

Goldman was known for his experiments involving "[[superconductivity]], in the configuration of thin films, with an emphasis on the effects of disorder and dimensional constraints."<ref name="nas" /> He did important research on properties of electron transport in them, and, especially, superconducting thin films (two-dimensional systems). In the mid-1980s, he and his group developed a new method for producing extremely thin superconducting films and used it to study the phase transition from superconductor to insulator in thin films, which became a prime example of a [[quantum phase transition]]. In addition to his research on superconductor-insulator transitions, he and his colleagues have studied "magnetic superconductors, heavy fermion materials, the investigation of the properties of [[High-temperature superconductor|high-''T''<sub>''c''</sub> superconductor]]s and the electrostatic control of the ground states of novel materials."<ref name="nas" /> He made important contributions, using [[molecular-beam epitaxy]], to the development of methods of producing high-''T''<sub>''c''</sub> superconductors.

From 1999 to 2005, he was an associate editor for the ''[[Reviews of Modern Physics]]''.<ref name="Allen Goldman" /> The University of Minnesota annually awards the Goldman Fellowship to a graduate student in the physics department.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Allen M. Goldman Fellowship |url=https://cse.umn.edu/physics/professor-allen-m-goldman-fellowship |website=School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Minnesota}}</ref>

In 2002, he received the [[Fritz London Memorial Prize]].<ref>{{cite news |author=Weisman, Wendy |date=August 2002 |title=U Professor receives award for low-temperature physics research |url=https://mndaily.com/188783/news/world/u-professor-receives-award-low-temperature-physics-research/ |newspaper=The Minnesota Daily (serving the UMN community since 1900)}}</ref>

From 2006 to 2008, he was vice-chair and then chair of the Division of Condensed Matter Physics of the American Physical Society.<ref name="AIP" />

In 2015, he received, jointly with [[Aharon Kapitulnik]], [[Arthur F. Hebard]], and [[Matthew P. A. Fisher]], the [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize]] for "discovery and pioneering investigations of the superconductor-insulator transition, a paradigm for quantum phase transitions."<ref name="BuckleyPrize" />

Goldman died on May 16, 2025, at the age of 87.<ref>{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam: Allen M. Goldman {{!}} School of Physics and Astronomy {{!}} College of Science and Engineering |url=https://cse.umn.edu/physics/news/memoriam-allen-m-goldman |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=cse.umn.edu |language=en}}</ref>
